title: Inverse image preserves allowable torsion
statement: Let U and V be schemes, let f:U → V be a morphism, let P be any set of natural numbers, and let F be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of V. If F has allowable torsion with prime divisors in P in the sense of [sbc-def-derived-categories-with-allowable-torsion], then the étale inverse image f⁻¹F has the same allowable-torsion property on U. There are no smoothness, quasi-compactness, or quasi-separatedness assumptions on f.

source.place: Existing private lemma allowable_upperStar, moved unchanged to a shared module so both bounded and bounded-below smooth base change reuse it.

proof.text: At any geometric point s:Spec Ω → U, use [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] to identify the stalk of f⁻¹F additively with the stalk of F at s ≫ f. Choose the positive allowable annihilator n of the image of the given stalk element. Additivity preserves multiplication by n and zero; injectivity of the comparison gives n times the original element equal to zero. Its positivity and allowed prime divisors are unchanged. This also covers P empty, where only the zero stalk elements can satisfy the hypothesis.
